key_insight: Rotor-slipstream modeling near the wing can reverse the predicted lift effect, outweighing the roughly 0.5% lift reduction from the kite’s helical wake.
engineering_relevance: Reliable wake predictions can inform airborne wind energy rotor integration and farm spacing, where a downstream kite lost 2.2% of aerodynamic power in the studied configuration.
method: Vortex step aerodynamics coupled to a time-marching free vortex wake in OpenFAWE.
Lumped-mass tether and actuator-disc rotors releasing vortex rings.
Single- and two-kite simulations comparing wake and slipstream treatments.
evidence_signal: Validation reproduced an independent vortex step code to 10^-9 for the M600 and within 0.3% in lift and 0.9% in drag for the V3 kite; V3 lift agreed with Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes results within 3.1%.
watch_item: Free rotor rings did not converge with time-step refinement, and alternative slipstream treatments predicted opposite lift changes (+1.9% versus −3.5%).
paper_title: Free-vortex-wake dynamics of airborne wind energy kites in crosswind flight
